@graph.name: End-of-Line Integration
@graph.description: End-of-line automation is the engineering of case packing, conveying and palletizing as one connected system, instead of separate machines bought from different suppliers and joined together during startup. TRF Industrial Automation designs, builds, installs and supports that complete line as one project, from the product to the finished pallet.

mainEntity.name: Can an End-of-Line Project Start With One Machine and Grow Later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each TRF palletizing and case packing platform can operate on its own and then integrate into a complete end-of-line system, with conveying added as an engineered system when volume grows. A plant can automate case packing first and complete the line with palletizing later. Planning the full flow at the start keeps each step compatible with the next one, including floor space, buffers and controls.

mainEntity.name: Does End-of-Line Automation Make Sense for a Lower-Speed Line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Palletizing starts at about 1 to 10 cases per minute with TRFCobot, and case packing covers applications from about 20 products per minute with TRFOnepack and TRFDroppack. Lower-speed lines often begin by removing manual case packing or hand palletizing, then connect the steps as volume grows, with each machine validated for its own application.

mainEntity.name: How Much Does an End-of-Line Automation Project Cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each integrated line is quoted for its full scope, because cost depends on the platforms selected, the number of lines, line speed, case weight, pallet pattern, conveyor length and routing, pallet handling and the interfaces with existing equipment. The robotic palletizer cost page explains the cost factors, and the payback calculator estimates payback for the palletizing step.

mainEntity.name: What Information Should I Prepare Before an End-of-Line Project Review?

acceptedAnswer.text: Prepare product dimensions, weight and packaging format for each SKU family; products per minute on each line and the number of lines; case dimensions, weight and pack pattern; pallet type, pattern and height; layout drawings with floor space, ceiling height, columns and aisles; shifts, planned growth and operating temperature; and the equipment the line must connect to.

mainEntity.name: What Support Is Available After an Integrated Line Starts Up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Technical support and a preventive maintenance program follow training and handover in every TRF project. Because one partner supplies the case packer, the conveyors and the palletizer, you deal with one company for the whole line. Parts and Service describes technical support, spare parts kept in the United States and the TRFCare preventive maintenance program.
